name: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd
title: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd - 540716 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: ICICI Lombard Q1 FY27 PAT fell 46.0% to ₹4.03 bn, driven by a ₹1.65 bn Motor TP judgement provision and two large Fire losses.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 GDPI grew 7.5% to ₹83.18 bn, below industry growth of 10.9%, with retail lines driving growth while commercial lines de-grew 13.8%. Combined ratio rose to 107.2% from 102.9%, including a 2.8 pp hit from the Supreme Court Motor TP judgement provision and a 1.0 pp hit from two Fire large losses. Excluding these items, the combined ratio was 102.3% versus 102.2% a year ago, and PAT would have been ₹5.75 bn (down 23.0%). Investment income fell to ₹11.74 bn from ₹12.88 bn as capital gains halved, partly offset by higher portfolio yield and duration.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: De-grew 13.8% in Q1 FY27 amid pricing pressure; SME share rose to 33.6% from 28.4%. Fire line declined 27.8% for the industry and the company de-grew about 32%; June Fire de-growth improved to about 18% for the company.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Grew 14.0% in line with industry (13.9%), market share 10.5%; new vehicle sales up 33.6% vs industry 14.9%. Mix: private car 49.8%, two-wheeler 28.7%, commercial vehicle 21.5%. Motor combined ratio 106.6% in FY26 vs industry 128.0%.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Grew 24.9% vs industry 20.1%. Retail Health grew 69.5% with share up to 4.5% from 3.5%; Group Health grew 16.3% with 10.3% share. Management attributed the higher health loss ratio to industry-wide claim incidence, not company-specific.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give a quantified forward impact of the Motor TP judgement; said it is too early and will update each quarter.
Expects an upward Motor TP premium rate revision; judgement-driven industry loss ratio impact estimated at 12-15%, which it sees as the minimum price change needed.
Expects Fire price aggression to moderate after Q1, though full recovery of de-growth in the rest of the year is uncertain.
Health claim incidence watch-point for Q2 (monsoon-linked); next detailed update to come with October results.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning plans were discussed on the call; the call covered underwriting, pricing, reserving and claims only.

Capacity was referenced only qualitatively: management said reinsurance renewals were relatively soft and capacity had been made available across the industry, which drove Fire price competition. No company-specific capacity figures were given.

Motor claims and servicing scale were cited as operating metrics, not capacity: Preferred Partner Network served 75.6% of non-OEM motor claims in Q1 FY27 vs 74.6% in Q1 FY26; 168,521 health and travel claims were serviced through the IL TakeCare app vs 141,116 a year earlier.
Digital servicing capacity: digital interactions rose to 624K in Q1 FY27 from 214K in Q1 FY26; digital share of servicing was 69.0% in Q1 FY27 and 71.0% in June 2026.
Management did not discuss any new product launches, branch or distribution expansion, or timelines for system or platform commissioning.
demand_pricing: Industry Fire rates were cut sharply in the April renewal cycle; the reinsurance renewal was relatively soft, enabling capacity and competition.
Motor TP has seen no third-party price change for several years; the judgement adds a Motor TP loss ratio impact of 12-15% for the industry.
Retail Health share gain: contribution from long-term book in new retail health business rose to 53.4% from 31.8%.
Digital interactions rose to 624K from 214K; digital share of servicing 69% in Q1 FY27 and 71% in June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ₹165 crore (₹1.65 bn) Motor TP provision only for Q1 business, and will it recur each quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the provision is a holistic assessment of exposures as at June 30, covering past book as well as Q1 business; it declined to say whether it will recur, citing variability in future quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the judgement affect closed cases, and what is the Fire loss ratio excluding the two large losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Closed cases typically do not reopen after court finality, so impact is largely on open exposures. Excluding the two large losses, Fire loss ratios should be within the historical 65-70% average range; the company has never exceeded 100% in Fire.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Health loss ratio rise despite GST benefit, and will it rise further in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects industry-wide higher claim incidence, similar to last year's Q1; it is watching monsoon-linked claims into Q2 and will update in October.

qa_highlights.question: Arbitration award of about ₹78 crore: provision and impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The award relates to a policy about seven to eight years old and is on a gross basis; the company will pursue legal remedies and believes the net P&L impact is not material given reinsurance.

qa_highlights.question: Will the reserve prudence buffer still generate releases given the ₹165 crore charge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its reserving philosophy is unchanged, prudence will continue, and reserving triangles should continue to show favourable development over cycles.

risks_watch: Motor TP judgement: outcome of the General Insurance Council review petition, the TP price revision, and whether provisions recur in Q2-Q4.
Fire pricing: competitive intensity and soft reinsurance renewals; watch whether industry de-growth narrows through the year.
Health loss ratio trend into Q2 with monsoon-linked claim incidence.
Possible regulatory change to Motor TP commission norms, not yet specified; management said it will wait for the regulator.
Arbitral award (about ₹78 crore plus interest) under legal challenge; contested by the company.
summary.management_tone: Confident on franchise and Motor underwriting relative to the industry, but notably cautious and non-committal on the forward Motor TP impact, repeatedly declining to quantify recurrence and deferring to later quarters.
key_quotes: Keeping with our prudent and conservative reserving practices, the Company has made an assessment of the impact of the judgement on its Motor TP portfolio and has made the requisite provisions in its financials for Q1 FY2027.
We are very confident in terms of saying that our reserving philosophy is holding us good, so there is no impact.
Our Motor combined ratio moved marginally to 106.6% in FY2026 from 105.3% in FY2025.
